abort.already_configured: This account or thermostat is already configured.
abort.wrong_device: That IP address belongs to a different thermostat.

error.cannot_connect: Nothing answered at this IP address. Check the IP in your router, and that Home Assistant can reach the thermostat's network (VLAN/firewall: TCP port 2000).
error.invalid_auth: Wrong email or password, or the account is blocked after too many wrong passwords.
error.not_a_thermostat: The device at this IP address answered, but not like a Saswell thermostat.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the logs for more info.
error.invalid_host: That's not a valid IP address. Enter it like 192.168.1.50.
error.unknown_host: No device with this name was found on your network. Enter the IP address instead (like 192.168.1.50).
error.connection_refused: A device answered at this IP address, but not on the thermostat port (2000). It's probably not the thermostat; check the IP.
error.no_answer: The thermostat at this IP address connected but didn't send its status. Try again in a moment.

user.title: Connection type
user.description: Local talks directly to one thermostat on your network (recommended, instant updates, no cloud). Cloud uses your Thermostat app account.

local.title: Local thermostat
local.description: Enter the thermostat's IP address. Give it a fixed IP (DHCP reservation) in your router. The thermostat must already be on your Wi-Fi. It works even if it no longer shows in the Thermostat app or your cloud account (this can happen after changing its Wi-Fi).

data_description.host: The thermostat's IP address on your network, for example 192.168.1.50. Find it in your router's list of connected devices.

cloud.title: Cloud account
cloud.description: Use the credentials from your Thermostat app. Note: the Saswell cloud only supports plain HTTP.

data_description.username: The email address you log in to the Saswell Thermostat app with.
data_description.password: The password of your Thermostat app account.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the password for {username}. Check that the account still works in the Thermostat app.

data_description.password: The current password of your Thermostat app account.

reconfigure.title: Change IP address
reconfigure.description: Enter the thermostat's new IP address.

data_description.host: The thermostat's IP address on your network, for example 192.168.1.50. Find it in your router's list of connected devices.

reconfigure_cloud.title: Update cloud password
reconfigure_cloud.description:
Enter the current password of the Thermostat app account {username}. Use this after changing the password in the app.

To use another account, add it as a new cloud hub.

data_description.password: The current password of your Thermostat app account.

data_description.scan_interval: How often Home Assistant asks the cloud for new values. Local thermostats don't use this; they send changes instantly.

move_to_local.title: Move thermostats to local control
move_to_local.description:
{count} thermostat(s) in {account} can be moved to local control:

{names}

On the next steps you enter the local IP address of each one. Leave the IP empty to keep that thermostat in the cloud.

A moved thermostat keeps its name, area, entity ID and history. Give each one a fixed IP address (DHCP reservation) in your router.

move_device.title: {name}
move_device.description:
Thermostat {index} of {total}: **{name}** (ID `{device_id}`).

Enter its local IP address to control it locally, or leave it empty to keep it in the cloud.

data_description.host: For example 192.168.1.50. Find it in your router's list of connected devices.

move_to_local.title: Move thermostats to local control
move_to_local.description:
Your thermostats can now be controlled directly on your network: instant updates, no cloud needed.

{count} thermostat(s) in {account} can be moved to local control:

{names}

On the next steps you enter the local IP address of each one. Leave the IP empty to keep that thermostat in the cloud.

A moved thermostat keeps its name, area, entity ID and history. Give each one a fixed IP address (DHCP reservation) in your router.

To keep using the cloud, close this and choose Ignore.
